title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit/Open
plain: The engine computer can't properly control the electronic throttle motor, which opens and closes the throttle when you press the gas pedal. It sees an open or broken circuit, often from wiring, a connector or the part itself.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor idle or slow response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Failed electronic throttle body
Broken wire or unplugged connector
Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the throttle body connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the electronic throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is commanding the electronic throttle to move, but the throttle isn't ending up where it should. A dirty or failing throttle body or a wiring problem is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Engine may idle high or stall
Slow or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Failing electronic throttle body (motor or gears)
Carbon buildup making the throttle plate stick
Loose or corroded throttle body connector
Damaged wiring between the throttle and computer
Low battery voltage or poor ground
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect and clean the throttle body bore and plate
Check the throttle connector and wiring
Check battery voltage and engine grounds
fix: Clean the throttle body and repair wiring; if the fault returns, replace the throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the electronic throttle motor is reading low voltage. This part opens and closes the throttle when you press the gas pedal. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor idle or slow response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Control wire shorted to ground
Internally shorted electronic throttle body
Damaged connector
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Check the throttle body wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the throttle body resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the electronic throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the electronic throttle motor is reading high voltage. This part opens and closes the throttle when you press the gas pedal. A wire shorted to power, an open circuit or a failed part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor idle or slow response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Failed electronic throttle body
Control wire shorted to a power source
Open circuit or corroded connector
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Check the throttle body wiring for shorts to other wires
Measure the throttle body resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the electronic throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Idle
plain: The engine computer has found a problem with the electronic throttle system and is protecting the engine by holding the engine at idle no matter how far you press the gas. Another throttle or pedal code usually explains why.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine stays at idle and won't speed up
Reduced engine power warning may show

causes.name: Throttle body or pedal sensor fault (see other stored codes)
Dirty or sticking throttle body
Wiring or connector problem at the throttle or pedal
Brake switch problem
Engine computer problem

checks: Read all stored codes and fix the other throttle or pedal codes first
Inspect the throttle body and its connector
fix: Repair the underlying throttle, pedal or wiring fault; this code clears once that is fixed.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Engine Shutdown

symptoms: Check engine light on

Reduced engine power warning may show

Engine computer problem

fix: Repair the underlying throttle, pedal or wiring fault; this code clears once that is fixed.

Reduced engine power warning may show

causes.name: Throttle body or pedal sensor fault (see other stored codes)

title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Processor
plain: The part of the computer that controls the electronic throttle has found an internal fault. The engine may go into limp mode to stay safe.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Engine may idle only

causes.name: Internal engine computer or throttle control module fault
Low system voltage or poor computer ground
Water damage to the computer
Software issue needing an update

checks: Check battery voltage, charging system and computer grounds
Check for software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix voltage or ground problems first; if the code returns, the computer may need reprogramming or replacement.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Performance
plain: The throttle control part of the engine computer isn't performing as expected. It's often triggered by voltage or wiring problems around the throttle system.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor throttle response

causes.name: Low battery or charging voltage
Poor computer ground
Throttle body fault
Internal engine computer fault

checks: Check battery and charging voltage and ground connections
Check for other throttle codes and service bulletins
fix: Correct voltage and ground problems; replace or reprogram the computer only after other causes are ruled out.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
plain: Throttle or pedal position sensor A isn't reading what the computer expects when the throttle or pedal is fully released. The resting position may be off or the sensor may be worn.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Idle too high or too low
Possible reduced power mode

causes.name: Carbon buildup keeping the throttle from closing fully
Worn throttle or pedal position sensor
Sticking pedal or throttle return spring
Throttle relearn not done after cleaning or battery disconnect

checks: Clean the throttle body and check that it closes fully
Run a throttle position relearn with a scan tool
fix: Clean the throttle and run a relearn; replace the throttle body or pedal if the reading is still off.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited RPM

Reduced engine power warning may show

causes.name: Throttle body or pedal sensor fault (see other stored codes)
Dirty or sticking throttle body
Wiring or connector problem at the throttle or pedal
Brake switch problem
Engine computer problem

checks: Read all stored codes and fix the other throttle or pedal codes first
Inspect the throttle body and its connector
fix: Repair the underlying throttle, pedal or wiring fault; this code clears once that is fixed.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Open
plain: The computer has found the electronic throttle stuck open and not moving when commanded. The engine may idle high or feel like it is surging.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
High idle
Engine may feel like it surges

causes.name: Sticking or failing electronic throttle body
Heavy carbon buildup on the throttle plate
Throttle motor wiring problem
Ice in the throttle body in freezing weather
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Look inside the throttle body for carbon or anything blocking the plate
Check the throttle connector and wiring
Clear the code and see if it returns after cleaning
fix: Clean the throttle body; if it still sticks or the code returns, replace the throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Closed
plain: The computer has found the electronic throttle stuck closed and not moving when commanded. The engine may have little power or stall.

Stalling or very low power

causes.name: Sticking or failing electronic throttle body
Heavy carbon buildup on the throttle plate
Throttle motor wiring problem
Ice in the throttle body in freezing weather

checks: Look inside the throttle body for carbon or anything blocking the plate
Check the throttle connector and wiring
fix: Clean the throttle body; if it still sticks or the code returns, replace the throttle body.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
plain: The electric motor that moves the throttle is drawing more or less current than expected. It may be binding, worn or have a wiring issue.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor throttle response

causes.name: Throttle motor binding from carbon or wear
Failing throttle motor
Wiring or connector fault
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Clean the throttle body and check that the plate moves freely
Inspect the throttle wiring and connector
fix: Clean the throttle; replace the throttle body if the motor is worn.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
plain: The throttle plate isn't returning to or holding the position the computer expects. Carbon buildup or a worn throttle body is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Rough or high idle
Stalling in some cases

causes.name: Carbon buildup on the throttle plate and bore
Worn or failing electronic throttle body
Weak throttle return spring
Wiring or connector problem
Ice in the throttle body in cold weather

checks: Inspect and clean the throttle body
Check the throttle connector and wiring
Check for service bulletins for your vehicle
fix: Clean the throttle body and run a relearn; if the code returns, replace the throttle body.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the throttle/pedal position sensor D, which helps tell the computer how far the gas pedal is pressed or how open the throttle is. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Faulty accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal)
Damaged, corroded or unplugged connector
Broken or chafed wiring
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the pedal or throttle sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal).

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The throttle/pedal position sensor D is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor helps tell the computer how far the gas pedal is pressed or how open the throttle is. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal)
A real fault in the system the sensor monitors
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the pedal or throttle sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal) if its readings are off.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
plain: One of the sensors that tells the computer how far you are pressing the gas pedal (sensor D) is reading lower voltage than expected. It's usually the pedal sensor or its wiring.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal
Possible stalling

causes.name: Failed accelerator pedal position sensor
Damaged wiring or connector at the pedal
Wire shorted to ground
Loose or corroded pedal connector
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the pedal connector and wiring under the dash
Watch pedal sensor readings while slowly pressing the pedal
Check the 5-volt reference and ground at the pedal
fix: Repair any wiring problems; otherwise replace the accelerator pedal assembly.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit High
plain: The signal from the throttle/pedal position sensor D is higher than the computer expects. This sensor helps tell the computer how far the gas pedal is pressed or how open the throttle is. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Unplugged or corroded connector
Failed accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal)
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the pedal or throttle sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal).

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the throttle/pedal position sensor D keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor helps tell the computer how far the gas pedal is pressed or how open the throttle is. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector
Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves
Failing accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal)

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the pedal or throttle sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the accelerator pedal position sensor (usually part of the pedal).

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/B Voltage Correlation
plain: Two position sensors that should agree with each other (sensors A and B) are giving different readings. On most cars these are the two sensors inside the throttle body.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal
Rough idle or stalling

causes.name: Failing electronic throttle body
Throttle sensor wiring or connector problem
Carbon buildup on the throttle
Shared 5-volt reference circuit shorted by another sensor
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the throttle body and pedal connectors for corrosion or loose pins
Watch both sensor readings together in live data while moving the throttle or pedal
Wiggle the harness while watching for dropouts
fix: Repair wiring or connector problems; otherwise replace the throttle body or pedal assembly, whichever holds the two sensors.
